chunks: And ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā and Zurʿah narrated from Samāʿah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about one who intentionally kills a believer: does he have repentance?

He said: "No, not until he pays his blood money to his family, frees a slave, fasts for two consecutive months, seeks forgiveness from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, repents to Him, and humbly implores; for I hope that repentance will be accepted from him if he does that."
I said: "May I be your ransom, what if he does not have wealth by which he can pay his blood money?"
He said: "He should ask the Muslims until he pays his blood money to his family."

key_terms.أَهْلِهِ: the victim’s family who are entitled to the payment
key_terms.تَوْبَةٌ: repentance; returning to Allah after grave sin
key_terms.دِيَتَهُ: the blood money owed for the killing
key_terms.رَقَبَةً: a slave to be freed as expiation
key_terms.يَتَضَرَّعَ: to humble oneself in earnest supplication

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about repentance for intentionally killing a believer?
ai.summary: This hadith states that repentance for intentionally killing a believer is not complete until the killer fulfills concrete obligations: paying the blood money to the victim’s family, freeing a slave, fasting two consecutive months, seeking Allah’s forgiveness, repenting, and showing humble supplication. If he lacks the means to pay the blood money, he is instructed to seek help from the Muslim community until he can fulfill that right.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5168 - Uthman ibn Isa and Zurah narrated from Samaah from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:
I asked Imam (as) about a person who intentionally kills a believer - does he have repentance?

Imam (as) said: "No, not until he pays the blood money (diyyah) to the victim's family, frees a slave, fasts for two consecutive months, seeks forgiveness from Allah (swt) the Almighty and Majestic, repents to Him (swt), and humbly supplicates.
I hope that if he does all of this, his repentance will be accepted."
I asked: "May I be your ransom, what if he has no wealth to pay the blood money?"
Imam (as) said: "Then he should ask the Muslims for help until he is able to pay the blood money to the victim's family."
